alice: Heads-up — saw a billing spike tied to a single customer stream. Looks like a reconnect + in-flight toolcall caused duplicate provisional ledger rows. 🧾

alice: Repro steps: start stream -> call tool (external fetch) -> client disconnects mid-toolcall -> client reconnects and resends, we accept and a second provisional charge appears, then finalization makes both provisional rows land as confirmed.

alice: Paste of relevant logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-19T17:02:11Z session=aa11 epoch=3 receiving TOOLCALL start id=tx-9abc
2026-03-19T17:02:13Z session=aa11 epoch=3 provisioning ledger: tx=tx-9abc tokens=48 provisional=true
2026-03-19T17:02:15Z session=aa11 disconnect reason=EOF
2026-03-19T17:02:17Z session=bb22 epoch=4 reconnect client_id=... resuming? false
2026-03-19T17:02:18Z session=bb22 epoch=4 receiving TOOLCALL start id=tx-9abc (replay)
2026-03-19T17:02:19Z session=bb22 epoch=4 provisioning ledger: tx=tx-9abc tokens=48 provisional=true
2026-03-19T17:02:21Z toolcall finished id=tx-9abc commit => both provisional rows reconciled -> charged
```

ben: Oof. So two provisional rows were keyed only by tx id but not by session epoch or realization id. When we reconcile we collapse on tx id and naively sum?

alice: Exactly. Our reconciliation path treats provisional rows as idempotent by tx id, but because the client replayed same tx id under a new session epoch we ended up double-applying.

ben: Quick thought: tie provisional entries to (tx id, session_epoch) and only collapse when commit includes that epoch. On reconnect we should expire provisional rows from old epoch if we detect a resumed-without-prefix.

carla: Agreed. Also the console UX needs to surface provisional vs confirmed clearly. Currently the billing dashboard just shows "Estimated" and then final. We should add event-level lines: pending provisional rows + reconciled delta. Something like: Pending: 48 tokens (session aa11, epoch 3) -> Reconciled: -48 / +0.

dan: From billing/legal side: if the double-charge hits customer we should auto-refund the duplicate. But we need a metric to detect these cases. Propose emitting `billing.provisional.unmatched` with tags {customer, model, route, delta_tokens} so we can alert and auto-remediate.

ben: Implementation note for runtime: when provisioning do: `provision_key = f"{tx_id}|{session_epoch}|{route}"` and on commit only collapse provisonals that match commit_epoch. For safety, have a grace TTL for old epoch provisonals (eg 5m) before auto-expire to cover slow commits.

alice: That matches my hack outline. Also we need to consider toolcall retries from clients that don't increment tx id. We can't rely on clients. So server-side should detect replay by matching same payload + different session epoch and mark as replay instead of new provisional.

carla: Console change: add new column in per-route timeline: `provisional_ids` showing session_epoch and tx snippets. And in the rollout dashboard, show provisional->committed deltas so SRE can see if a new routing policy spike correlates to reconnections.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: eng-runtime hotfix canary @staging at 2026-03-20T02:00Z; eng-console patch @staging at 2026-03-20T03:30Z.

dan: Once hotfix lands we should run a regression job: simulate reconnects and ensure ledger net tokens unchanged. I'll add a smoke test in billing CI.

ben: One more micro edge: KV cache eviction can cause client to replay because model context truncated -> same symptoms. TTL on provisional rows needs to be >= typical reconnect window. Let's default to 10m but make it configurable per-customer.

alice: Action items: 1) ben -> runtime PR to include session_epoch in provisional key + TTL config. 2) carla -> console patch to show provisional ids and delta. 3) dan -> metric + refund automation proposal. 4) alice -> write the e2e test and schedule canary.

alice: TLDR: double provisional on reconnect due to missing session_epoch in ledger key. Patch + UI + metric + refund automation.

carla: :eyes: thanks for the clear logs.

ben: I'll start a draft PR and tag you all.

alice: thx. :thumbsup:
